checks._why: unmark() is what makes a re-run a rebuild rather than an append. Without it the second run stacks a second managed block onto every page, and this program has now been run twice on the same 35 pages, so the failure would be live rather than hypothetical.

checks.find: const appliedLive = applied && (!verified || verified.has(applied.handle)) ? applied : null;
checks._why: This is the guard that kept round one honest: with it off the generator emits all 35 cards whatever the storefront says, and 17 of them would have pointed at a 404. The safety is in the fixture and this line is what consults it.

checks.name: 18 of the 35 rebuild BYTE FOR BYTE as published, which is the proof a re-run is safe
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),os=require('os');const {OPEN}=require('./scripts/extract-live-body');const D='smoke/fixtures/csp-lesson-bodies-round2';const t=fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(),'csp2-'));for(const f of fs.readdirSync(D))if(f.endsWith('.html'))fs.writeFileSync(path.join(t,f),''+OPEN+fs.readFileSync(path.join(D,f),'utf8')+String.fromCharCode(10)+' ');const {build}=require('./scripts/csp-lesson-exercise-links');const v=new Set(fs.readFileSync('smoke/fixtures/csp-verified-handles-round2.txt','utf8').split(String.fromCharCode(10)).map(s=>s.trim()).filter(Boolean));const r=build(t,v);if(r.problems.length)throw new Error(r.problems[0]);if(r.pages.length!==35)throw new Error('built '+r.pages.length);const same=r.pages.filter(p=>p.body===p.original).length;const applied=r.pages.filter(p=>p.applied).length;if(applied!==35)throw new Error('expected 35 applied cards, got '+applied);if(same!==18)throw new Error('expected 18 byte-identical, got '+same);console.log('REBUILD FAITHFUL 18 byte-identical, '+(35-same)+' rows written, 35 applied cards');"
checks._why: The 18 pages that already carry a correct managed block must come out of a fresh run identical to what the storefront serves, so they fall out of the sheet on their own. That is idempotence demonstrated against live bytes rather than asserted.
